## Nepal Sanskrit University
                             
  Compulsory English Courses
                               Level: Shastri Second Year

Course Title: Reading and Writing across the Curriculum
Code: Comp. Eng. 402                             Full Marks: 100
Teaching Hours: 150                                Pass Marks: 40

Course Description: The purpose of the course is to develop reading and writing competence
among the students. Students will familiarize themselves with discourses from different
disciplines. Once the diverse texts are read, students will attempt to summarize, critique, analyze,
synthesize, and reflect upon such readings. Through practice, students will also acquaint
themselves with the fundamental principles of usage of English language. Finally, the course aims
to prepare them for advanced level of reading and writing skills essential for academic and
professional life.


UNIT I: Usage, Composition, and Style                                  30 hrs.
        Rules of Usage
        Principles of Composition
        Matters of Form
        Words and Expressions Commonly Misused
        An approach to Style

UNIT II: Reading and Writing Summaries and Critiques                   30 hrs.
         Summary, Paraphrase, and Quotation
         Critical Reading and Critique
         Introductions, Theses, and Conclusions

UNIT III: Reading and Writing Syntheses and Analyses                    30 hrs.
          Explanatory Synthesis
          Argument Synthesis
          Analysis

UNIT IV: Economics, Environment/ Public Policy, Sociology               30 hrs.
         Readings:
             Ursula Huws. "Fixed and Footloose Work and Identity in the
                  Twenty-First Century"
             Thomas Friedman. "The Untouchable"
             Lubber Mindy. "Balance Sheets and Climate Crisis: How American
                  Business can Help"
             Michael Totty. "The Case for and Against Nuclear Power"
             Stephanie Coontz. "The Radical Idea of Marrying for Love"

Eric Bartels. "My Problem with Her..."
